configs.name: lean-order-number-semijoins
configs.rationale: Smallest, cheapest-to-build set: order-number indexes on the catalog/web sales and returns tables so the correlated EXISTS / NOT EXISTS and IN subqueries in q16, q94 and q95 become index nested-loop semi/anti joins instead of full hash joins.

configs.name: secondary-date-and-time-keys
configs.rationale: Targets the fact-table date/time foreign keys that have no index yet (ship dates, return dates, sold time) so date_dim/time_dim-driven filters in q16/q94/q95/q62/q99, the returns-side filters in q1/q5/q17/q25/q29/q50, and the time-of-day scans in q88/q90/q96 can use index nested loops instead of seq scans.

configs.name: dimension-filter-indexes
configs.rationale: Leaves the big fact tables alone and instead indexes the selective dimension predicates (d_year/d_moy, d_month_seq, d_date, d_week_seq, t_hour, and the marital/education/gender filters on the 1.9M-row customer_demographics) so the many repeated dimension subqueries and lookups become index-only scans with very low build cost.

configs.name: balanced-recommended
configs.rationale: Mid-size set combining the highest-ROI items: order-number semi-join indexes for q16/q94/q95, the store_sales time/hdemo/store index for q88/q96, ship-date indexes on catalog/web sales, and a covering returned-date index on store_returns, all with modest build times.

configs.name: aggressive-covering-facts
configs.rationale: Accepts large build times for wide covering indexes on the three sales facts keyed by (sold_date, item) with the most-used measures INCLUDEd so date- and item-driven aggregates can run as index-only scans, plus an item-leading inventory index to turn the inventory joins in q37/q72/q82 into index lookups, and the order-number and time indexes for the semi-join and time-of-day queries.
